entities.summary:
Deutsche Lufthansa AG is the flag carrier of Germany, founded in 1926 with predecessor roots in the Weimar Republic era. Europe's largest airline group by revenue and passengers, the Lufthansa Group encompasses Swiss International Air Lines, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines, Eurowings, and a 40% stake in ITA Airways (Alitalia's successor).

Lufthansa was dissolved after WWII as part of Allied restrictions, then re-established in 1953 in West Germany, becoming a symbol of postwar German economic revival. Its MUC (Munich) and FRA (Frankfurt) hubs grew into major European transfer points rivaling Heathrow and Amsterdam. Lufthansa's acquisition strategy — absorbing national carriers of Germany's neighbors — created a Central European aviation empire.

The COVID-19 pandemic required a €9 billion German government bailout to prevent bankruptcy, making Germany a 25% shareholder temporarily. The German government's reacquisition of a stake mirrored debates globally about strategic industries and state support during crises. Lufthansa's Technik division, one of the world's largest aircraft maintenance providers, and LSG Sky Chefs, the world's largest airline catering company (partially sold), demonstrate vertical integration in aviation beyond passenger services.
